records.source: Διὸ ἀφέντες τὸν τῆς ἀρχῆς τοῦ Χριστοῦ λόγον ἐπὶ τὴν τελειότητα φερώμεθα, μὴ πάλιν θεμέλιον καταβαλλόμενοι μετανοίας ἀπὸ νεκρῶν ἔργων, καὶ πίστεως ἐπὶ θεόν, βαπτισμῶν διδαχὴν ἐπιθέσεώς τε χειρῶν, ἀναστάσεώς τε νεκρῶν καὶ κρίματος αἰωνίου.
records.gloss: Therefore having left the of the beginning of the Christ word to the perfection let us be carried, not again foundation laying down of repentance from dead works, and of faith toward God, \v 2 of washings teaching, of laying on and of hands, of resurrection and of dead [ones] and of judgment eternal.
pieces: So let us leave behind the first message about {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} and be carried forward to maturity. Let us not be laying a foundation all over again: turning away from dead works and putting faith in God,
teaching about ritual washings and the laying on of hands, the raising of the dead and eternal judgment.

L.1: Therefore, having left the word of the beginning of the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, let us be carried on to perfection, not laying down again a foundation of repentance from dead works and of faith toward God,
L.2: teaching about washings and laying on of hands, and resurrection of [the] dead and eternal judgment.

R.1: So let us move past the first lessons about {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} and grow up. We do not need to lay the foundation again. That foundation is turning away from works that bring death and putting our faith in God.
R.2: It includes teaching about ritual washings and about laying hands on people, about the dead being raised, and about God's eternal judgment.

decisions.choice: the word of the beginning of Christ: the first, basic teaching about Christ
alternatives: the teaching Christ himself first gave
decisions.reason: The phrase restates "the elements of the beginning" in 5:12. "Of Christ" is most naturally the teaching about Christ, the first things believers are taught about him.

decisions.choice: perfection: maturity, the grown-up understanding of 5:14
decisions.reason: τελειότητα picks up "the perfect" (the mature) of 5:14 and belongs to the same word family as "made perfect" in 5:9. The goal is full understanding of the faith, here the teaching of Christ's priesthood.

decisions.choice: let us be carried on: let us move forward, carried along
alternatives: let us press on by our own effort
decisions.reason: φερώμεθα is passive in form: "let us be carried". It can simply mean "let us move on", but the passive leaves room for being borne along by God, which fits verse 3 ("if God permits").

decisions.choice: dead works: deeds that lead to death, done apart from the living God
alternatives: the rituals of the old covenant
good works done to earn salvation
decisions.reason: The phrase comes again in 9:14, where Christ's blood cleanses the conscience "from dead works to serve the living God". It means sinful deeds that belong to death, from which a person turns in repentance. Some read it of the rituals of the law, which cannot give life; 9:14 favors deeds that defile the conscience.

decisions.choice: teaching: in the accusative, standing alongside "a foundation"
alternatives: of teaching: a further item in the list depending on "foundation"
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT reads διδαχὴν, so "teaching" restates the foundation: the foundation consists of the teaching about washings and the rest. Many manuscripts have the genitive form instead, which makes it one more item in the list. The sense hardly changes. This note is written from general knowledge of the manuscripts; reviewers must check it against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: washings: ritual washings, including the distinction between Christian baptism and other washings
alternatives: the washing at baptism and the inner washing of the heart
decisions.reason: βαπτισμῶν is plural and is the word for washings in general; 9:10 uses it for the washings of the law and Mark 7:4 for washing cups and pots. The usual word for Christian baptism is a different one. A foundational teaching about "washings" may have explained how baptism differs from Jewish purifications and from John's baptism. The plural makes a simple "baptism" unlikely, but the exact reference is uncertain.

decisions.choice: laying on of hands: a sign of blessing, of receiving the Spirit, and of commissioning
decisions.reason: In the Old Testament hands were laid on for blessing and commissioning (Genesis 48:14; Numbers 27:18-23). In the early church the act went with prayer for the Spirit (Acts 8:17; 19:6), with healing (Acts 28:8), and with sending people out for a task (Acts 6:6; 13:3; 1 Timothy 4:14).

decisions.choice: the foundation: six basic teachings in three pairs, already laid and not to be laid again
alternatives: teachings to be left behind as unimportant
decisions.reason: The list falls into pairs: turning from dead works and faith toward God; washings and laying on of hands; resurrection and eternal judgment. All of them have roots in Israel's Scriptures and were taught to new believers. The author does not discard them; a foundation stays in place, but one does not keep relaying it. The call is to build on it.

decisions.choice: maturity (Balanced), grow up (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "perfection" to show the link with 5:9 and 5:14; Balanced and Readable say "maturity" and "grow up", as at 5:14.

decisions.choice: ritual washings
decisions.reason: "Ritual" makes clear these are religious washings, not ordinary bathing, while leaving open which ones (see the meaning decision).

decisions.choice: works that bring death
decisions.reason: Readable explains "dead works" according to the meaning decision: deeds that lead to death.

records.source: καὶ τοῦτο ποιήσομεν ἐάνπερ ἐπιτρέπῃ ὁ θεός.
records.gloss: And this we will do if indeed permits the God.
pieces: And we will do so, if God allows.

L.3: And this we will do, if only God permits.

R.3: And we will go on, if God lets us.

decisions.choice: this: going on to maturity
decisions.reason: "This" most naturally takes up the main call of verse 1, "let us be carried on to maturity". The author then goes on to give fuller teaching himself (chapters 7-10).

decisions.choice: we will do: future
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT reads the future ποιήσομεν, "we will do". Some manuscripts have the very similar subjunctive, "let us do", which would make it a further call. The difference in spelling is one letter. This note is written from general knowledge of the manuscripts; reviewers must check it against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: if God permits: progress depends on God
decisions.reason: The condition prepares for verses 4-6: going forward is God's gift, and the author will warn about those for whom there is no way back.

decisions.choice: we will go on
decisions.reason: Readable names what "this" refers to, according to the meaning decision.

records.source: Ἀδύνατον γὰρ τοὺς ἅπαξ φωτισθέντας γευσαμένους τε τῆς δωρεᾶς τῆς ἐπουρανίου καὶ μετόχους γενηθέντας πνεύματος ἁγίου καὶ καλὸν γευσαμένους θεοῦ ῥῆμα δυνάμεις τε μέλλοντος αἰῶνος, καὶ παραπεσόντας, πάλιν ἀνακαινίζειν εἰς μετάνοιαν, ἀνασταυροῦντας ἑαυτοῖς τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ παραδειγματίζοντας.
records.gloss: Impossible for the [ones] once having been enlightened having tasted and of the gift of the heavenly and sharers having become of spirit holy \v 5 and good having tasted of God word powers and of coming age, \v 6 and having fallen away, again to renew to repentance, crucifying again for themselves the son of the God and exposing to shame.
pieces: There are those who have once been enlightened, who have tasted the gift from heaven, who have received a share in the Holy Spirit,
who have tasted that God's word is good and have tasted the powers of the coming age,

and who have then fallen away. It is impossible for them to be brought back again to repentance, as they crucify the Son of God over again for themselves and put {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to open shame.

L.4: For [it is] impossible [for] those once having been enlightened, and having tasted the heavenly gift, and having become sharers of [the] Holy Spirit,
L.5: and having tasted [that the] word of God [is] good, and [the] powers of [the] coming age,
L.6: and having fallen away, to renew [them] again to repentance, crucifying again for themselves the Son of God and exposing [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}] to open shame.

R.4: Think of people whose eyes were once opened to the light. They tasted the gift that comes from heaven. They received their share of the Holy Spirit.
R.5: They tasted how good God's word is, and the powers of the age that is coming.
R.6: Then they turned away. It is impossible to bring them back again so that they turn from their sins. They are nailing the Son of God to the cross again for themselves and putting {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to open shame.

decisions.choice: the warning states that those who have shared these gifts and then fall away cannot be brought back to repentance; it does not answer the further questions readers bring to it
alternatives: true believers can lose their salvation
the case is hypothetical, to warn and not to describe anyone
it is impossible for people to restore them, but not for God
decisions.reason: The passage says plainly that for people who have shared richly in the gifts listed and have then fallen away, renewal to repentance is impossible. It does not say whether such people were truly saved, whether anyone among the readers had done this, or whether the impossibility is for human teachers or absolute. Christians have answered these questions in different ways, and the text leaves them open. What the author does say is that he is confident of better things for his readers (6:9-12). Compare the warnings in 2:1-3, 3:12-14, 10:26-31 and 12:15-17. The translation renders the words as they stand and does not settle these questions.

decisions.choice: enlightened, tasted, sharers: real experiences of the gospel and the Spirit
decisions.reason: "Enlightened" is used again in 10:32 for the readers' coming to the faith. "Tasted" means to experience something; in 2:9 Jesus "tasted death", which was real. "Sharers" is the word of 3:1 and 3:14, where the readers are "sharers" of a heavenly calling and of Christ. How far these experiences go is part of the open question in the theology decision; the words themselves describe real experience. ἅπαξ means "once", in the sense of once for all.

decisions.choice: they tasted that God's word is good
alternatives: they tasted the good word of God
decisions.reason: "Good" stands apart from "word" in the Greek and reads as a statement about it: they found by experience that what God says is good. Joshua 21:45 and 23:15 speak of the "good word" God promised and kept, and Psalm 34:9 invites people to taste and see that the Lord is good.

decisions.choice: the powers of the coming age: the miracles and works of the Spirit that belong to the world to come
decisions.reason: In 2:4 God confirmed the message with signs, wonders and various "powers" and gifts of the Holy Spirit. The author calls them powers of the coming age because they are a foretaste of the world to come (2:5).

decisions.choice: fallen away: turned away from Christ, abandoning the faith
decisions.reason: παραπεσόντας is not a single lapse but a turning away. The rest of the verse explains it: siding with those who crucified the Son of God and holding him up to contempt. Compare 3:12, "turning away from the living God", and 10:26-29, deliberate sin that tramples the Son of God underfoot.

decisions.choice: it is impossible to renew them again to repentance: the person who would renew them is not named
alternatives: impossible for teachers like the author
decisions.reason: The infinitive ἀνακαινίζειν has no stated subject. The Greek leaves open whether human teachers cannot bring such people back or whether it cannot happen at all; see the theology decision. The translation keeps the subject unstated at every level.

decisions.choice: crucifying again
decisions.reason: In ordinary Greek ἀνασταυροῦντας simply means to crucify, literally to raise up on a cross. Early Christian readers understood it here as "crucify again", which suits the context ("again" in the same verse, and the readers' first coming to faith), and the translation follows that sense.

decisions.choice: as they crucify: the participles describe what they are doing while they fall away, and give the reason renewal is impossible
alternatives: as long as they crucify (a time limit only)
decisions.reason: The participles ἀνασταυροῦντας and παραδειγματίζοντας are present: an ongoing action. They may give the reason ("since they are crucifying") or the time ("while they keep crucifying"). If the second, the impossibility lasts as long as they persist in rejecting him. The Greek allows both, and the translation keeps the link loose.

decisions.choice: for themselves ... put him to open shame
decisions.reason: "For themselves" can mean "to their own harm" or "as far as they are concerned". παραδειγματίζοντας means to make a public example of someone, to expose to disgrace, as crucifixion itself did.

decisions.choice: description first, then "it is impossible"
alternatives: it is impossible for those who have ... to be brought back
decisions.reason: The Greek puts "impossible" first and the long description after it. Balanced and Readable describe the people first and then state the impossibility, so the sentence can be followed when read aloud. Balanced uses "to be brought back", which, like the Greek, does not say who brings them.

decisions.choice: whose eyes were once opened to the light
decisions.reason: Readable explains "enlightened" in plain words.

decisions.choice: so that they turn from their sins
decisions.reason: Readable explains "repentance" as turning from sin.

records.source: γῆ γὰρ ἡ πιοῦσα τὸν ἐπ’ αὐτῆς ἐρχόμενον πολλάκις ὑετόν, καὶ τίκτουσα βοτάνην εὔθετον ἐκείνοις δι’ οὓς καὶ γεωργεῖται, μεταλαμβάνει εὐλογίας ἀπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ·
records.gloss: Land for the having drunk the upon it coming often rain, and producing vegetation useful to those for whom also it is tilled, partakes of blessing from the God;
pieces: When the ground drinks in the rain that falls on it again and again and yields plants that serve the people who work it, it shares in God's blessing.

L.7: For land that has drunk the rain often coming upon it and produces vegetation useful to those for whose sake it is also farmed, shares in blessing from God;

R.7: Think of a field. Rain falls on it again and again. If it grows plants that are useful to the farmers who work it, God blesses it.

decisions.choice: for: the picture of the field explains the warning of verses 4-6
decisions.reason: The same rain falls on all the ground; what differs is what the ground produces. The rain answers to the gifts of verses 4-5, and the crops or thorns to what people do with them.

decisions.choice: receives blessing from God: God makes it fruitful
decisions.reason: In Israel's Scriptures rain and good harvests are God's blessing on the land (Genesis 27:27; Deuteronomy 11:11-15; Psalm 65:10-14).

decisions.choice: Think of a field ... If
decisions.reason: Readable introduces the picture as a picture and turns the long participle phrase into short sentences with "if", which the contrast with verse 8 implies.

records.source: ἐκφέρουσα δὲ ἀκάνθας καὶ τριβόλους ἀδόκιμος καὶ κατάρας ἐγγύς, ἧς τὸ τέλος εἰς καῦσιν.
records.gloss: bringing forth but thorns and thistles [it is] worthless and of curse near, of which the end [is] for burning.
pieces: But if it brings up thorns and thistles, it is rejected as worthless and a curse is close at hand; it will finish by being burned.

L.8: but bringing forth thorns and thistles, [it is] worthless and near to a curse, whose end [is] for burning.

R.8: But if it grows thorns and thistles, it is no good. It is close to being cursed, and at last it will be set on fire.

decisions.choice: thorns and thistles near a curse: Genesis 3:17-18
decisions.reason: After the first sin God cursed the ground, and it brought forth "thorns and thistles" (Genesis 3:17-18). The picture of a vineyard that yields bad fruit and is laid waste is also in Isaiah 5:1-7.

decisions.choice: worthless: tested and rejected
decisions.reason: ἀδόκιμος is used of what fails a test and is thrown out (compare 1 Corinthians 9:27; 2 Corinthians 13:5).

decisions.choice: near to a curse, whose end is burning: judgment is close but is described as the end of a process
decisions.reason: The land is "near" a curse, not yet under it, which leaves room for the hope of verse 9. "Whose" refers to the land. Farmers burned off useless growth; the author uses it as a picture of judgment by fire (10:27; 12:29).

decisions.choice: at last it will be set on fire
decisions.reason: Readable makes "its end is for burning" a simple statement about what will happen.

records.source: Πεπείσμεθα δὲ περὶ ὑμῶν, ἀγαπητοί, τὰ κρείσσονα καὶ ἐχόμενα σωτηρίας, εἰ καὶ οὕτως λαλοῦμεν·
records.gloss: We have been persuaded but concerning you, beloved, the better [things] and holding [to] salvation, if even thus we speak.
pieces: Yet about you, dear friends, we are confident of better things, things that come with salvation, even if we talk this way.

L.9: But we have been persuaded of better things concerning you, beloved, and things belonging to salvation, even if we speak this way.

R.9: But dear friends, even though we talk like this, we are sure that things are better with you. We are sure you have the things that go with being saved.

decisions.choice: we are persuaded: the author speaking of himself; a settled conviction
decisions.reason: As in 5:11, "we" is the author's own voice over against "you". Πεπείσμεθα is perfect: "we have become convinced and remain so".

decisions.choice: things belonging to salvation: what goes with being saved
decisions.reason: ἐχόμενα with a genitive means "holding to, connected with". It answers verse 8: the land there is "near a curse"; the readers' lives show things that go with salvation, as verse 10 explains.

decisions.choice: better things
decisions.reason: "Better" is a favorite word of Hebrews: a better name (1:4), a better hope (7:19), a better covenant (7:22; 8:6), better promises and sacrifices (8:6; 9:23). Here it contrasts the readers with the land of verse 8.

decisions.choice: dear friends
decisions.reason: ἀγαπητοί is the only time the author calls the readers "beloved". "Dear friends" carries the warmth in present-day English and includes men and women. Literal keeps "beloved".

records.source: οὐ γὰρ ἄδικος ὁ θεὸς ἐπιλαθέσθαι τοῦ ἔργου ὑμῶν καὶ τῆς ἀγάπης ἧς ἐνεδείξασθε εἰς τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ, διακονήσαντες τοῖς ἁγίοις καὶ διακονοῦντες.
records.gloss: Not for unjust [is] the God to forget the work of you and the love which you showed toward the name of him, having served the saints and serving.
pieces: For God is not so unfair as to forget your work and the love you have shown for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name by serving {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holy people, and by serving them still.

L.10: For God [is] not unjust to forget your work and the love which you showed toward {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name, having served the saints and [still] serving [them].

R.10: God is not unfair. He will not forget the work you have done, or the love you showed for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} when you helped {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people. And you are still helping them.

decisions.choice: God is not unjust so as to forget
decisions.reason: The infinitive gives the result that would follow if God were unjust: forgetting what they have done. Because God is just, he will not forget it. This is not a claim that their work earns salvation; it is evidence of the "things belonging to salvation" (verse 9).

decisions.choice: toward his name: toward him
decisions.reason: God's "name" stands for God himself. Love shown to his people is love shown to him (compare Matthew 25:40).

decisions.choice: serving the saints: helping fellow believers, God's holy people
decisions.reason: "The saints" are all believers, people set apart for God, not a special class. 10:32-34 describes how the readers stood by those who were imprisoned and lost their property; 13:1-3 calls for the same care.

decisions.choice: his holy people (Balanced), his people (Readable)
decisions.reason: "Saints" today often suggests especially holy individuals; the Greek means all who belong to God. Literal keeps "the saints".

decisions.choice: for him
decisions.reason: Readable gives the sense of the idiom "his name" (see the meaning decision).

records.source: ἐπιθυμοῦμεν δὲ ἕκαστον ὑμῶν τὴν αὐτὴν ἐνδείκνυσθαι σπουδὴν πρὸς τὴν πληροφορίαν τῆς ἐλπίδος ἄχρι τέλους, ἵνα μὴ νωθροὶ γένησθε, μιμηταὶ δὲ τῶν διὰ πίστεως καὶ μακροθυμίας κληρονομούντων τὰς ἐπαγγελίας.
records.gloss: We desire but each of you the same to show earnestness toward the full assurance of the hope until end, \v 12 so that not sluggish you become, imitators but of the [ones] through faith and patience inheriting the promises.
pieces: Our desire is that each of you show the same eagerness right to the end, until your hope is fully assured.
Then you will not grow sluggish; you will follow the example of those who, by faith and patience, are receiving the promises as their inheritance.

L.11: But we desire each of you to show the same earnestness toward the full assurance of the hope until [the] end,
L.12: so that you may not become sluggish, but imitators of those who through faith and patience are inheriting the promises.

R.11: We want every one of you to keep working just as hard to the end, so that you will be fully sure of what you hope for.
R.12: We do not want you to become lazy. Copy those who have faith and patience, and so receive what God promised.

decisions.choice: the full assurance of the hope: being fully certain of what is hoped for
alternatives: the full realization of the hope
decisions.reason: πληροφορίαν can mean full certainty or full measure. In 10:22 it is the "full assurance of faith". The readers are to keep the same zeal they showed in serving (verse 10) so that their hope stays certain to the end.

decisions.choice: sluggish: the same word as in 5:11
decisions.reason: The adjective of 5:11 returns and closes the section. There the readers had become sluggish in hearing; here the author wants them not to become sluggish in hope and action.

decisions.choice: those who through faith and patience inherit the promises: believers who wait in trust for what God promised, Abraham first of all
decisions.reason: The present participle describes people who are inheriting the promises. The next verses give Abraham as the example, and chapter 11 lists many more. Faith and patience go together: trusting God and waiting for him to act.

decisions.choice: follow the example of
decisions.reason: "Imitators" is the literal word; Balanced says "follow the example of", which is how English speaks of copying a good model.

decisions.choice: We do not want you to become lazy. Copy those ...
decisions.reason: Readable makes the purpose clause of verse 12 into a separate sentence and a direct call, so the long Greek sentence becomes short ones.

records.source: Τῷ γὰρ Ἀβραὰμ ἐπαγγειλάμενος ὁ θεός, ἐπεὶ κατ’ οὐδενὸς εἶχεν μείζονος ὀμόσαι, ὤμοσεν καθ’ ἑαυτοῦ, λέγων· Εἰ μὴν εὐλογῶν εὐλογήσω σε καὶ πληθύνων πληθυνῶ σε·
records.gloss: To the for Abraham having promised the God, since by no one he had greater to swear, he swore by himself, \v 14 saying: Surely blessing I will bless you and multiplying I will multiply you.
pieces: God made a promise to Abraham, and having no one greater to swear by, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} took an oath by {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}},
saying, "Truly I will bless you richly and multiply you greatly."

L.13: For God, having made a promise to Abraham, since {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} could swear by no one greater, swore by {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}},
L.14: saying, "Surely, blessing I will bless you, and multiplying I will multiply you."

R.13: God made a promise to Abraham. There was no one greater than God for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to make an oath by, so {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} made an oath by {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}.
R.14: He said, "I will surely bless you, and I will give you very many descendants."

decisions.choice: Genesis 22:16-17
decisions.reason: After Abraham was ready to offer Isaac, God said, "By myself I have sworn", and promised to bless him and multiply his offspring (Genesis 22:16-17). Genesis says "I will multiply your offspring"; the author quotes it as "I will multiply you", keeping the focus on Abraham himself. The doubled verbs ("blessing I will bless") copy a Hebrew way of giving emphasis: "I will surely bless".

decisions.choice: surely: a formula used for oaths
decisions.reason: Εἰ μὴν is a fixed formula in Greek for a solemn assurance, "most certainly".

decisions.choice: God swore by himself because there is no one greater
decisions.reason: An oath calls on someone greater to guarantee one's word (verse 16). God has no one above him, so he pledged his own being (Genesis 22:16; compare Isaiah 45:23).

decisions.choice: I will give you very many descendants
decisions.reason: Readable states what "multiply you" means: a great number of descendants, as Genesis 22:17 has it.

decisions.choice: no one greater than God
decisions.reason: Readable names God in the comparison so the reason for the oath is clear.

records.heading: God's promise and God's oath

records.source: καὶ οὕτως μακροθυμήσας ἐπέτυχεν τῆς ἐπαγγελίας.
records.gloss: And thus having waited patiently he obtained the promise.
pieces: And so, after waiting with patience, Abraham obtained the promise.

L.15: And so, having waited patiently, he obtained the promise.

R.15: Abraham waited patiently, and so he received what God had promised.

decisions.choice: he obtained the promise: he received God's sworn word and saw it begin to be fulfilled
alternatives: he received all that was promised
decisions.reason: Abraham waited many years for Isaac, and after the test of Genesis 22 God confirmed the promise with an oath. Yet 11:13 and 11:39 say that Abraham and the others died without receiving what was promised in full. So "obtained the promise" here most likely means he received the promise confirmed and its first fulfillment (Isaac's birth and his return from the altar), not everything it held.

decisions.choice: Abraham
decisions.reason: The Greek says "he"; Balanced and Readable name Abraham so the reader does not take "he" as God, the subject of the verses before.

records.source: ἄνθρωποι γὰρ κατὰ τοῦ μείζονος ὀμνύουσιν, καὶ πάσης αὐτοῖς ἀντιλογίας πέρας εἰς βεβαίωσιν ὁ ὅρκος·
records.gloss: Men for by the greater swear, and of all for them dispute an end for confirmation the oath;
pieces: Human beings swear by one greater than they are, and for them an oath settles every dispute, because it confirms what is said.

L.16: For {{gender:people|men}} swear by the greater [one], and for them the oath [is] an end of every dispute, for confirmation;

R.16: When people make a promise, they swear by someone greater than themselves. The oath proves they mean it, and that ends every argument.

decisions.choice: confirmation: a legal guarantee
decisions.reason: βεβαίωσιν was used for a legal guarantee that makes something valid and binding. An oath was the final word in a dispute because it called on a higher power to back the speaker's word.

decisions.choice: {{gender:people|men}}
decisions.reason: ἄνθρωποι here means human beings in general, so the gender setting applies at Literal. Balanced says "human beings" and Readable "people", which need no setting.

decisions.choice: When people make a promise
decisions.reason: Readable supplies the setting of an oath, which the next verse makes clear: God's oath backs up his promise.

records.source: ἐν ᾧ περισσότερον βουλόμενος ὁ θεὸς ἐπιδεῖξαι τοῖς κληρονόμοις τῆς ἐπαγγελίας τὸ ἀμετάθετον τῆς βουλῆς αὐτοῦ ἐμεσίτευσεν ὅρκῳ, ἵνα διὰ δύο πραγμάτων ἀμεταθέτων, ἐν οἷς ἀδύνατον ψεύσασθαι θεόν, ἰσχυρὰν παράκλησιν ἔχωμεν οἱ καταφυγόντες κρατῆσαι τῆς προκειμένης ἐλπίδος·
records.gloss: In which more abundantly desiring the God to show to the heirs of the promise the unchangeableness of the purpose of him guaranteed by oath, \v 18 so that through two things unchangeable, in which impossible to lie God, strong encouragement we may have the [ones] having fled for refuge to take hold of the being set before hope;
pieces: So God, wanting the heirs of the promise to see all the more clearly that {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} purpose would never change, added an oath to guarantee it.
He did this so that through two things that cannot change, and in which God cannot possibly lie, we who have fled for refuge would have strong encouragement to seize the hope placed before us.

L.17: In which [matter], God, wanting to show even more fully to the heirs of the promise the unchangeableness of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} purpose, guaranteed [it] by an oath,
L.18: so that through two unchangeable things, in which [it is] impossible [for] God to lie, we who have fled for refuge might have strong encouragement to take hold of the hope lying before [us];

R.17: God wanted to show the people who would receive what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} promised that {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} plan would never change. So {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} made {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} promise sure with an oath.
R.18: God cannot lie, and these two things, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} promise and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} oath, can never change. So we who have run to find safety are strongly encouraged to hold on to the hope set in front of us.

decisions.choice: guaranteed it by an oath: God stood between as guarantor of his own promise
decisions.reason: ἐμεσίτευσεν is from the same family as the word for "mediator" (8:6; 9:15; 12:24). It means to act as a go-between or a guarantor. God, who had no one greater to call on, put his own oath between himself and the heirs as a pledge.

decisions.choice: two unchangeable things: God's promise and God's oath
alternatives: the oath to Abraham and the oath of Psalm 110:4
decisions.reason: Verses 13-17 speak of a promise backed by an oath, so the two things are most naturally the promise and the oath. The author goes on to make much of the oath of Psalm 110:4 (7:20-22), but that is not yet in view here.

decisions.choice: it is impossible for God to lie
decisions.reason: God does not lie or change his mind (Numbers 23:19; 1 Samuel 15:29; Titus 1:2). The same word "impossible" was used in verse 4; here it is the ground of the readers' confidence.

decisions.choice: we who have fled for refuge: perhaps an echo of the cities of refuge
decisions.reason: καταφυγόντες is used of fleeing to a place of safety. The law set apart cities of refuge where someone in danger could flee and be safe (Numbers 35:9-15; Deuteronomy 19:1-10), and the picture may be in mind; but the author does not develop it.

decisions.choice: strong encouragement to take hold of the hope
alternatives: we who have fled in order to take hold of the hope
decisions.reason: "To take hold" can go with "encouragement" (encouragement to hold on to the hope) or with "having fled" (fled to lay hold of the hope). The sense is close either way. The translation links it with encouragement. "Set before us" uses the same verb as 12:1-2, the race and the joy set before.

decisions.choice: added an oath to guarantee it
decisions.reason: Balanced gives the sense of the go-between word (see the meaning decision) in everyday language.

decisions.choice: his promise and his oath
decisions.reason: Readable names the two unchangeable things, according to the meaning decision.

records.source: ἣν ὡς ἄγκυραν ἔχομεν τῆς ψυχῆς, ἀσφαλῆ τε καὶ βεβαίαν καὶ εἰσερχομένην εἰς τὸ ἐσώτερον τοῦ καταπετάσματος, ὅπου πρόδρομος ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν εἰσῆλθεν Ἰησοῦς, κατὰ τὴν τάξιν Μελχισέδεκ ἀρχιερεὺς γενόμενος εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα.
records.gloss: which as anchor we have of the soul, secure both and firm and entering into the inner of the curtain, \v 20 where forerunner on behalf of us entered Jesus, according to the order Melchizedek high priest having become to the age.
pieces: This hope is ours as an anchor for the soul, one that holds safe and firm and reaches into the inner place behind the curtain.
There Jesus entered ahead of us and for our sake, as a forerunner, having become a high priest forever, of the order of Melchizedek.

L.19: which we have as an anchor of the soul, both secure and firm, and entering into the inner [place] of the curtain,
L.20: where a forerunner on our behalf entered, Jesus, having become a high priest forever according to the order of Melchizedek.

R.19: This hope is like an anchor for our souls. It holds us safe and steady. It reaches behind the curtain into the most holy room.
R.20: Jesus has already gone in there ahead of us and for us. He has become a high priest forever, the kind of priest Melchizedek was.

decisions.choice: which ... entering: the hope, pictured as an anchor, reaches into the inner sanctuary
alternatives: the anchor alone, apart from the hope
decisions.reason: ἣν refers back to "the hope" of verse 18. The participle εἰσερχομένην agrees with the hope and the anchor: the hope is fixed where Jesus has gone, as an anchor holds a ship to something firm out of sight.

decisions.choice: anchor: a picture of security
decisions.reason: An anchor keeps a ship from drifting (compare "drift away" in 2:1). In the ancient world it was a common picture of steadiness and hope. The author mixes the picture with the sanctuary: the anchor holds in heaven itself.

decisions.choice: the inner place behind the curtain: the Most Holy Place, Leviticus 16:2, 12, 15
decisions.reason: In Leviticus 16 the high priest went "inside the curtain" into the Most Holy Place once a year on the Day of Atonement. The author applies this to the heavenly sanctuary into which Jesus has entered (9:11-12, 9:24; 10:19-20).

decisions.choice: forerunner on our behalf: one who goes ahead so that others may follow
decisions.reason: πρόδρομος is one who runs ahead, such as a scout or an advance runner. The high priest of Israel entered the Most Holy Place alone and the people stayed outside; Jesus goes in ahead so that his people can follow (10:19-22; compare 2:10, the "pioneer" who leads many children to glory).

decisions.choice: Psalm 110:4 again
decisions.reason: The verse closes the section by returning to Psalm 110:4, quoted in 5:6 and named in 5:10. Chapter 7 takes it up in full.

decisions.choice: curtain
decisions.reason: καταπετάσματος is the curtain in the sanctuary that closed off the Most Holy Place (Exodus 26:31-33). "Curtain" is the plain word; "veil" is the traditional one.

decisions.choice: behind the curtain into the most holy room
alternatives: into the inner place behind the curtain
decisions.reason: Readable names the room the phrase means, according to the meaning decision (Leviticus 16).

decisions.choice: of the order of Melchizedek (Balanced); the kind of priest Melchizedek was (Readable)
decisions.reason: As at 5:6 and 5:10.
